hits.excerpt: In mathematics, the cobordism hypothesis, due to John C. Baez and James Dolan,[1] concerns the classification of extended topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). In 2008, Jacob Lurie outlined a proof of the cobordism hypothesis, though the details of his approach have yet to appear in the literature as of 2022.[2][3][4] In 2021, Daniel Grady and Dmitri Pavlov claimed a complete proof of the cobordism hypothesis, as well as a generalization to bordisms with arbitrary geometric structures.[4]

hits.excerpt: The Cobordism Hypothesis establishes an equivalence between fully extended Topological Quantum Field Theories (TQFTs) and symmetric monoidal functors from a category of cobordisms to a target category, often vector spaces or higher categories. It formalizes the idea that a TQFT is completely determined by its value on a point, subject to dualizability conditions. This reduces the classification of TQFTs to algebraic data associated with manifolds of minimal dimension.
